reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns LCO effects on irradiation resistance in CrCoNi and passivation in CoCrFeMnNi high/medium-entropy alloys, not 316L stainless steel. No evidence is provided to support the key premises that thermal aging induces LCO in 316L, that such LCO forms Cr-rich nanoclusters, or that it enhances corrosion resistance in this alloy. The premises are thus unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Thermal aging at 500–600 °C promotes LCO in 316L stainless steel
LCO in 316L manifests as Cr-rich nanoclusters
LCO enhances passivation by forming a more uniform, Cr-rich passive film
LCO lowers mobility of corrosive species and accelerates passive film formation
LCO-driven passivation improvement reduces corrosion rate and pit density
